meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Federal Jurisdiction, Canada (Canada Business Corporations Act)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid federal legal system: federal corporate law is statutory and interpreted under common-law principles; Quebec private law follows civil law; federal incorporation coexists with provincial corporate and tax registration.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada's Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreements (FIPAs) in force with more than 35 counterparties
Canada's network of bilateral income tax conventions (DTAAs) with more than 90 jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, as amended, ss. 19 and 21.1-21.6; Canada Business Corporations Regulations, SOR/2001-512; Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, as amended; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, s. 462.31; related FINTRCA regulations and anti-money-laundering policy directions.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access: the CBCA significant-control register is maintained privately at the registered office and must be produced to the Director of Corporations Canada, FINTRAC, law enforcement, or other authorized regulators upon lawful demand; it is not currently a fully public federal register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or national identity document of each director, incorporator, and individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or competent issuing agency in the country of residence, further certified by a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the originating country's competent authority; for non-Hague countries, Canadian consular legalization through the Canadian embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address such as a utility bill, tax notice, or bank statement for each individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, tax authority, or bank in the country of residence, with notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on whether the country of origin is an Apostille Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency, corporate authorization, or notarized corporate resolution when an individual with significant control is a legal entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry, corporate secretary, or registered agent of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certificate of corporate status plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization from the relevant foreign competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/KYC bank reference letter from the relationship bank showing account standing, source of funds, and identified beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Compliance officer or authorized corporate banker of the foreign relationship bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized officer signature with Hague Apostille or consular legalization; if issued in Canada, notarization and an apostille from Global Affairs Canada

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC-compliant AML/CFT program includes: non-face-to-face identification and verification of all directors, shareholders, and individuals with significant control; determination of domestic and foreign politically exposed persons and heads of international organizations; senior management approval and source-of-wealth/source-of-funds documentation for PEPs; screening against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, and Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; screening against UN Security Council resolutions, OFAC SDN list where USD payment rails are used, and FATF high-risk jurisdiction alerts; all positive hits and negative news refer to legal counsel before incorporation proceeds.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre / NUANS Name Search Portal (Newly Updated Automated Name Search) through Corporations Canada and authorized NUANS service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A federal corporate name may be in English, French, or bilingual English-French form. The name must include a legal element such as Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, Ltée, Inc., Corp., or a statutory abbreviation. Names not written in the Latin alphabet must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet before filing. The selected language form is applied consistently to the corporate seal, articles, and negotiated instruments.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Insurance, Assurance, Loan, Finance: require prior approval of the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions or the applicable provincial financial regulator
Royal, Crown, Government, Federal, Provincial, Municipal, Her Majesty: imply Crown or governmental patronage and require ministerial consent
University, College, Institute of Technology, Polytechnic: require designation or consent of the responsible provincial education ministry
Engineer, Professional Engineer, Architect, Geoscientist: require prior authorization from the applicable provincial regulator for regulated professions
Lawyer, Attorney, Barrister, Solicitor, Notary Public: require the approval of the relevant provincial law society or notarial licensing authority
Hospital, Clinic, Health Centre, Pharmaceutical: may require proof of regulatory authorization and will generally be reserved for licensed health sector users
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name request is refused, Corporations Canada issues written reasons. The applicant may submit a reconsideration request within a reasonable administrative timeline, ordinarily 30 days, attaching a written consent from the conflicting name holder, evidence of trademark registration, or a revised distinctive element. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant must file a new NUANS search and name reservation. Where statutory grounds exist, the applicant may apply to the Federal Court for judicial review of the Director of Corporations Canada's decision under the Federal Courts Act and applicable CBCA provisions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only as a managed physical address. CBCA section 19 requires the registered office to be a fixed street address in the province named in the articles; a post office box alone is not acceptable. A lawyer's office or a professional registered-office service at a physical street address is compliant and recommended for an affiliate media-buying corporation with no Canadian staff. A purely virtual mailbox arrangement without service-of-process capability is not compliant. Books and records must remain accessible to directors and regulators at a disclosed location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: approximately 8% estimated probability of a Canada Revenue Agency audit, records inspection, or GST/HST/payroll compliance visit within the first 24 months of digital advertising operations. Unannounced physical inspection of the registered office is not routine; however, failure to maintain the significant-control register or to produce books and records on demand may trigger compliance orders and escalated regulatory inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 8, 9, 19, 21, 28, 97-98, 106, 113, 124; Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001, SOR/2001-512
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Industry, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) — Federal Incorporation Portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) filed via the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre; accompanied by the NUANS Name Search Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; CBCA permits no-par-value common shares and deferred consideration for share subscription; no escrow account requirement under federal incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation adopts its Articles of Incorporation as filed and directs management to obtain federal registration from Corporations Canada. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Corporation allots and subscribes for one hundred (100) no-par-value common shares to the founding subscriber on deferred payment terms permitted by the CBCA. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office shall be at the address stated in the Notice of Registered Office, and that the individuals identified in the Statement of Directors be appointed directors. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary are appointed officers of the Corporation, each authorized to execute agreements.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada via a registered NUANS search agent; online submission at corporations-canada.ic.gc.ca
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) corporate name report through an approved service provider. Review the preliminary name for distinctiveness and file the Name Reservation Request via the Corporations Canada portal to secure a 90-day name reservation notice. If the proposed name is refused for confusion or clarity, revise the corporate name and submit a second reservation request.
required_dossiers: Credit card or direct debit authorization for fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit a second NUANS search using a distinctive trademark or corporate style; if refused on clarity grounds, add a legal element or revised distinctive word and re-file; appeal an administrative name refusal to the Director under s. 12 CBCA within the applicable statutory window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Director General, Corporations Canada, ISED — Online Filing Centre
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 4001 by entering the company name, registered office address, share structure (authorized no-par-value common shares), director list and any restrictions on business. Pay the filing fee online and submit electronically. Upon clearance, Corporations Canada issues a Certificate of Incorporation evidencing creation of the federal legal entity.
required_dossiers: NUANS reservation number or approved name report
Initial registered office address in Canada
Names, addresses and signatures of initial directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct deficiencies flagged by the online system and resubmit; if the filing is queried for missing director consents, file the director consent forms and continue; no post-incorporation cure is required once the certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notice of Registered Office and Board of Directors (Form 4002/4003)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada, ISED — Federal Registration Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of incorporation, file the Notice of Registered Office (Form 4002) and Notice of Directors (Form 4003), or incorporate the same data within the initial filing. Ensure the registered office is a physical address in Canada (not a post office box) and that each director satisfies CBCA eligibility (individual, at least 18 years of age, not bankrupt, and at least 25% of directors resident in Canada).
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director for each appointee
Statement of director residence for Canadian residency requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File an amended notice via the Corporations Canada online portal if the initial notice is queried; any late-filing concern may be cured by immediate submission and payment of the assessed late fee, with no substantive loss of corporate status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Board Resolution and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (internal records; no governmental filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first meeting of directors or pass written resolutions in lieu of a meeting pursuant to the CBCA. Approve the corporate by-laws, appoint the Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary, approve bank account forms and signing authorities, authorize issuance of common shares to the founding subscriber, and ratify the registered office lease.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting or consent to written resolution
Bank account opening package and signing authority resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a quorum cannot be reached, call an adjourned meeting and confirm minutes by resolution; any defect in an officer appointment may be cured retroactively by a subsequent board resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Share Issuance and Maintenance of Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Corporate Secretary (internal corporate records; register within the securities register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue the subscribed common shares, record them in the corporation's share register, deliver share certificates, and maintain the register of directors and registered office filings. Prepare the corporate records book as required under ss. 20-24 CBCA for inspection by the Director or shareholders upon demand.
required_dossiers: Notice by directors of change of residence where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any clerical defect in share registration by board resolution and reissue certificates; missing register entries may be reconstructed from corporate records and statutory declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number, GST/HST, and Payroll Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, apply for the federal Business Number via the CRA's Business Registration Online portal. Register for the GST/HST account if annual taxable supply revenue exceeds CAD 30,000, and open a payroll deduction account if employees are hired. Establish a corporate bank account under the legal corporate name.
required_dossiers: Employer and beneficial owner identification for beneficial ownership reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Registration is instantaneous online; if the Business Number is not issued automatically, call the CRA business inquiries line or submit Form RC1A/RC1 manually; provincial tax discrepancies may be referred to the relevant provincial/territorial authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial or manufacturing authorization required for ISIC 7310 performance media buying activity
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable (no federal or provincial operating permit for digital advertising brokerage or affiliate media buying)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / Federal Environmental Assessment Coordinator
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical works or undertakings triggering the Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero wastewater discharge, VOC emissions or hazardous waste streams from software-based media buying; if an office lease is executed, landlord building systems must comply with applicable municipal plumbing, electrical and HVAC codes

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy compliance: municipal fire safety inspection for the leased office, structural load confirmation under the applicable provincial building code, and provincial/territorial occupational health and safety clearance (e.g., Ontario OHSA) for workstations, electrical safety and emergency exits; no special civil defense permit required for remote media buying operations

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – federal tax administration; GST/HST registration and filing through CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO) portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register for a Business Number (BN), the de facto TIN for corporations, via CRA's Business Registration Online or Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number). Non-resident corporations without a place of business in Canada may file Form RC1E. For GST/HST purposes, add a GST/HST program account to the BN on the same registration or by writing to the relevant CRA tax centre. The BN is a 9-digit number followed by a two-character program identifier (e.g., RC0001). Registration must be obtained before charging GST/HST in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian resident and non-resident corporations are separate taxable entities under Part I of the Income Tax Act; no look-through treatment is available for federal income tax purposes).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a U.S.-style check-the-box classification regime. Permanent combinations: corporations are always taxed as corporations. Elections that may be relevant include the S.216 election for non-residents receiving Canadian rental income to be taxed on net taxable income rather than gross Part XIII tax, elections respecting foreign affiliate status under the S.95 foreign affiliate regime, and specified hybrid mismatch election forms added by Canada's BEPS Action 2 implementation. No general pass-through election exists for Canadian corporations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST), administered federally under the Excise Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in total annual worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies for most persons; a non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada is required to register for GST/HST once its taxable supplies sourced to Canada exceed this small supplier threshold, subject to specific exceptions (e.g., supplies of excluded property, or supplies deemed not carried on business in Canada).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing in Canada. GST/HST registrants must retain and issue invoices containing prescribed particulars (BN, invoice date, description, amount, and GST/HST rate and amount). Electronic invoices are permitted if they are accessible and readable by the CRA. Mandatory electronic GST/HST return filing applies to registrants with taxable supplies in excess of CAD 1.5 million, but this is not a transaction-level clearance requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for goods requires physical export from Canada by the supplier or on its behalf, and evidence that the goods were shipped to a destination outside Canada; supplies of services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident of Canada and not rendered primarily in connection with real property situated in Canada or tangible personal property located in Canada (or the service is performed wholly outside Canada). Digital advertising, affiliate media buying, and lead-generation services supplied to non-residents will normally be zero-rated as intangible property/services if not referable to Canadian situs property.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: B13A Canada Customs Export Declaration (or CES/CAED equivalent with detailed goods description and value)
Commercial Invoice or Supplier Invoice including Canadian business number, description, quantity, value, and zero-rating indicator
Bill of Lading or other shipping/transport evidence showing export from Canada and destination outside the customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT/MT103 wire confirmation, or other proof of payment receipt from the foreign buyer to substantiate the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits may require full due diligence on every zero-rated supply, including proof of export, non-resident status, and payment documentation. If the documentation is insufficient or the commercial substance is found to reflect a round-trip financing arrangement, the CRA may deny zero-rating, reassess GST/HST at the standard rate plus interest, and levy penalties under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act (5%–10% of the amount if uncorrected, or a higher civil penalty of 25% for knowingly making a false statement). For corporate income tax, such arrangements may also attract transfer-price reassessments, Part XIII withholding and penalties, and general anti-avoidance rule application under the Income Tax Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Foreign-exchange regulation in Canada is liberalized under the Currency Act R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52; the former Foreign Exchange Control Act has been repealed and no dedicated foreign-exchange administration or exchange-control permit authority currently exists. OSFI supervises all Schedule I banks; FINTRAC enforces the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) at the transactional reporting layer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is freely convertible on both current and capital accounts under a market-determined free float. Capital repatriation, dividend distribution, and profit remittance to non-resident parents require no BOC or OSFI approval; the sole fiscal impediment is Part XIII withholding tax of the Income Tax Act (25% statutory, reducible to 5% or 15% under an applicable income tax treaty, e.g., the Canada-U.S. Convention, subject to limitation-on-benefits provisions). The Investment Canada Act (ICA) applies only to non-Canadian investments exceeding the WTO enterprise-value threshold (CAD 1.095 billion as of the 2024 annual adjustment for non-cultural businesses; CAD 5 million direct / CAD 50 million indirect for cultural businesses). Digital advertising media arbitrage (ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810) is non-cultural and typically falls below all ICA filing thresholds unless foreign control of a Canadian cultural enterprise is established. No exchange-control contracts, licensing, or by-law approvals are required for inbound or outbound treasury flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose any statutory timeline for repatriation of export/advertising-services proceeds, nor any mandatory conversion ratio for foreign-currency receipts. Affiliate media-buying revenues may be retained indefinitely in USD, CAD, or any convertible currency. Reporting obligations remain applicable: (i) FINTRAC Large Cash Transaction Report (LCTR) for cash receipts over CAD 10,000; (ii) FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) for inbound/outbound wire and ACH transfers of CAD 10,000 or more in a 24-hour period; (iii) Common Reporting Standard (CRS) and FATCA account disclosures; and (iv) CBCA annual return declarations of foreign beneficial ownership.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operating Account (CAD) with USD sub-ledger and Lynx wire connectivity
Enterprise Operating Account (CAD) plus TD US Dollar Money Market account and TD Bank (U.S.) ACH bridge
Dual-currency Operating and Settlement Account (CAD/USD) with BMO Harris cross-border corridor
Global Transaction Banking Account (CAD) with LATAM and U.S. payment corridors
Operating Account plus Capital Escrow Account (CAD) for intercompany equity injection

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as an ancillary payout rail; Medium as sole primary banking. Wise Business (Canada) operates as a FINTRAC-registered Money Services Business (MSB) through Canadian partner banks and offers low-cost multi-currency accounts with segregated client funds; Payoneer maintains a Canadian MSB license and supports publisher/affiliate payouts to 70+ countries. Legal constraints: any fintech EMI must be registered as an MSB under the PCMLTFA before client onboarding, must execute its own LCTR/EFTR reporting obligations, and cannot provide deposit insurance (CDIC) nor extend credit or overdraft facilities. Mercury (U.S.-chartered, non-branch foreign bank) is not viable as a primary operating account for a CA-FED entity; it may only serve as an upstream treasury account at the U.S. parent level, with the Canadian subsidiary settling through a Schedule I bank. Recommended architecture: RBC or TD as the primary settlement bank, with Wise Business sub-accounts for low-value publisher payouts where SWIFT per-transaction costs exceed rail economics.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted at RBC, TD, BMO, and CIBC for Canadian-incorporated private companies. Directors are NOT required to appear physically; banks accept a video-conference KYC interview with a Corporate Onboarding officer, electronic identity verification via Equifax/TransUnion credit-bureau checks, and notarized or commissioned corporate resolutions. Mandatory elements: identification of all ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) holding 25% or more of shares or voting control; a sanctions/PEP declaration signed by a director with Canadian nexus; IRS Form W-8BEN-E or W-9 for any U.S. beneficial owner; and a 160-character corporate-purpose questionnaire describing the affiliate media-buying model. No statutory license is required for media buying, and no CIRO/dealer registration applies to the treasury function. Non-resident directors without a Canadian address must appoint an authorized signatory resident in Canada or engage a registered corporate-service provider for records service.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency ACH and wire outflows to a large cohort of individual publisher and affiliate payees, flagged under 'sunburst' or structuring typologies without contractual counterparty documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved publisher payout register with lead/pixel volume metrics; signed Publisher Services Agreements governing commission rates, payment terms, and clawback mechanics; ad-server click and impression logs (Google Ads, Meta Ads, programmatic DSP reports) reconcilable to each invoice; UBO and director CDD packs; a written Anti-Money Laundering / Sanctions policy; and a documented FINTRAC Compliance Program satisfying section 71 PCMLTFA obligations if the entity's payment flows trigger MSB classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial wires to or from high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., offshore ad networks in jurisdictions with known AML deficiencies) for media placements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial justification memorandum with rate-card benchmarks; executed media-buying and reseller agreements; vendor KYC pack containing beneficial-ownership, business-license, and bank-reference documentation; OFAC/UN/EU/Canada sanctions screening results archived to the due-diligence file; and a controlled distribution list identifying each destination account by legal name and jurisdiction, provided to the relationship manager for quality assurance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intercompany equity injection or parent-level capital transfer flagged for round-tripping, tax-evasion structuring, or unsupported exempt purpose (e.g., a USD capital contribution routed through intermediate holding entities).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed intercompany loan agreement or subscribed-share resolution confirming the corporate purpose; Board minutes authorizing the injection; contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation under Income Tax Act section 247 establishing arm's-length equity terms; a Part XIII withholding-position memorandum identifying the applicable treaty rate; and a section 12 PCMLTFA EFT report receipt where the aggregate transfer equals or exceeds CAD 10,000.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing protocol: (1) Inward remittance from the U.S. parent to the RBC or TD Operating Account via SWIFT MT103, with field 23E purpose code '7020' (capital to subsidiary) and field 70 REMITTANCE INFO stating 'SUBORDINATED LOAN' or 'EQUITY CONTRIBUTION'; (2) instruct the receiving bank to retain USD in a dual-currency sub-ledger, or execute a same-day spot conversion to CAD at the bank's retail-trade rate with the FX contract recorded in the treasury system; (3) onward domestic movements settled through the Lynx large-value payment system (Payments Canada successor to LVTS) or the ACSS for sub-threshold amounts; (4) for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, the bank files the FINTRAC EFTR and the entity must avoid structuring to evade reporting; (5) document the contribution in the CRA corporate register and evaluate a section 85.1 share-for-share rollover or section 86 reorganization if preferred-equity instruments are used. Director identification must match the mandate registration filed under the CBCA; the ICA, if a non-Canadian investor is acquiring control, triggers only above the annual enterprise-value threshold and is inapplicable to a USD 500,000–2,000,000 seed round.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail: SWIFT MT103 wire to the publisher/agency beneficiary bank for all cross-border trade settlements, funded through the USD sub-ledger to avoid double FX conversion; domestic publisher payouts above CAD 10,000 routed via Lynx; payouts below CAD 10,000 via ACSS (automated EFT/ACH) or Interac e-Transfer for micro-affiliates; Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) are generally inapplicable to pure-service media buying but may be used if goods-linked lead-generation arrangements (e.g., trial offers with physical fulfilment) arise. Settlement instructions must contain the beneficiary's legal-name match and BIC11 identifier; the bank will block transfers to parties on the Canadian, OFAC, UN, and EU sanctions lists; FX volatility is neutralized either by converting the expected payout batch into USD at the Bank of Canada daily average rate on the same day or by executing a forward contract before vendor invoicing. Retain MT103 confirmation messages and recipient bank acknowledgements for CRA and FINTRAC audit trail purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/CAD deliverable FX forwards (custom tenors 1–12 months, executed OTC under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex or cleared through CDCC)

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on USD/CAD with non-resident bank counterparties, permitted where hedging intent can be documented and where such instruments are used solely to offset CAD/USD exposure from media-buying receivables
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD) for matched intercompany balance-sheet hedging of the USD capital base and long-term affiliate receivables
Plain-vanilla FX options (OTC calls or puts on the USD/CAD pair) to protect payout-batch operating margin while retaining upside participation
Rolling spot forward contracts (time options) providing flexible settlement windows when publisher invoice timing is uncertain

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or continuation, each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a CAD $100 late-filing charge on top of the CAD $12 online fee; failure to file for one year or more allows the Director to administratively dissolve the corporation, with revival requiring filing of all omitted returns, a prescribed application, and a reinstatement fee.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of each taxation year (fiscal year-end); financial statements and all supporting schedules must accompany the T2
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; a repeat failure triggers 10% plus 2% per month; daily compound interest on unpaid balances; arbitrary reassessment under the Income Tax Act and possible criminal prosecution for wilful failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing period assigned by the CRA at registration: monthly (due within 1 month after month-end), quarterly (due within 1 month after quarter-end), or annual (due within 3 months after fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 1% of net tax due plus 25% of that penalty when a prior failure occurred within the preceding 24 months, capped at CAD $1,000 for non-annual filers and CAD $2,500 for annual filers; daily compound interest and CRA arbitrary assessment apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T4 Statement and T4 Summary of Remuneration Paid (and T4A for reportable commissions or fees)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the last day of February following each calendar year for paper filing, or March 1st for electronic filing; employee copies must be provided by the same deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of CAD $100 per information slip per late day, capped at 75% of the amounts that should have been withheld; additional penalties under section 162 of the Income Tax Act and possible prosecution for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM), Director and Shareholder Resolutions, and Presentation of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records maintained at the registered office; no government filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM within 18 months of incorporation and thereafter within 15 months of the previous AGM, and in any event no later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A shareholder may apply to court under CBCA section 127 to compel an AGM; directors who fail to convene the meeting or maintain statutory records may face compliance orders and fines of up to CAD $5,000 on summary conviction.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the CBCA, every business corporation must appoint an auditor at its first and each subsequent annual meeting; the audit may be dispensed with only by unanimous shareholder resolution each fiscal year for a non-distributing corporation. No small-company revenue or asset exemption exists under the CBCA. Distributing (public) corporations cannot waive the audit, and a shareholder or group holding at least 5% of the outstanding voting shares may apply to a court to require an independent auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) is mandatory for distributing corporations; ASPE (Part II) is available to private non-distributing corporations; financial statements must be prepared under generally accepted accounting principles and laid before the AGM.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the CBCA Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) regime, the corporation must update the ISC register within 15 days after any share transfer or change of significant control. When filing the CBCA annual return, the filing officer must confirm that the ISC register is complete and accurate. Share transfers must be approved by the directors, recorded in the Register of Transfers, and reflected in the Register of Members before the annual confirmation is submitted.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 190-900 per year (CAD 250-1,200) typical for CBCA registered office and corporate agent services, inclusive of provincial extra-provincial registrations where the media-buying affiliate carries on business
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000-15,000 per year (CAD 5,000-20,000) for a non-distributing digital advertising and affiliate media-buying operating company; a lower-cost review engagement may be acceptable only if the statutory audit is validly waived by unanimous shareholder consent.

stage_6.entry_description: Enter the legal name, address, jurisdiction of incorporation, fiscal year-end date (YY-MM-DD), and total revenue from financial statements (IFRS/ASPE).
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation filing Part I tax uses the same T2 and must include only income from its Canadian business/net of treaty PE allocation; list the Canadian permanent establishment address in the identification box.
